rubriker.title: Wesley So Wins 2026 Us Chess Championship
US Championship 2026: Tiebreak!
rubriker._rss_content: The 2026 U.S. Championship came to a dramatic conclusion: Wesley So lost to last-placed Sam Sevian in the final round, ending his 48-game unbeaten streak at the U.S. Championships. Fabiano Caruana, meanwhile, won on demand against Awonder Liang to catch So at the top of the standings. The title will now be decided in a playoff, beginning with two rapid games at 15+10. If the scores remain level, another two rapid games will follow, then up to two two-game blitz matches at 5+2. If the players are still tied, the arbiter will decide how to proceed. | Live with commentary from 12.00 CDT / 18.00 BST / 19.00 CEST | Photo: Crystal Fuller

rubriker.title: US Chess Championships 2026 - Games and results
rubriker._rss_content: The US Chess Championships took place in Saint Louis Fri 9th Oct to Wed 21st Oct 2026. Wesley So won his fourth title after a tie-break win against defending champion Fabiano Caruana (winner the last four years 2022-25 champion). So had led by a point from Caruana going into the final round but lost to tail-ender Sam Sevian. The women's event was of great interest too with debutant Rachael Li winning on her first time out, half a point clear of Alice Lee.

rubriker.title: Rachael Li Wins 2026 Us Womens Chess Championship
Rachel Li wins US Women's Championship on her debut
rubriker._rss_content: Going into the final round of the 2026 US Women’s Championship in St Louis, Rachael Li was the sole leader with 8 points from 10 games, one point ahead of Alice Lee. Li therefore needed only a draw against Anna Zatonskih in the final round to win the tournament. Li secured both the draw and the title, becoming US Women's Champion at just 16 years of age. She also collected $45,000 in prize money, qualified for the next Women's World Cup and earned her first IM norm. | Photo: Lennart Ootes / Saint Louis Chess Club

rubriker.title: 2026 European Chess Club Cup Round 4
European Club Cup Rounds 3 and 4: Abdusattorov, Giri and Erdogmus All Lose
rubriker._rss_content: The European Chess Club Cup in Budva, Montenegro reached its halfway point with upsets in both sections. In the open, Round 3 belonged to the favorites, with 15-year-old Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus climbing to world No. 15, before Round 4 saw Nodirbek Abdusattorov, Anish Giri and Erdogmus all lose. In the women's, CE Gambit Bonnevoie beat both of the top two seeds in a row and leads alone on a perfect 8 match points.

rubriker.title: All new releases in September!
rubriker._rss_content: The latest releases offer fresh ideas for opening preparation and regular chess training. In two volumes, Michael Kotyk presents a practical repertoire for Black after 1.e4 e5, while Fabien Libiszewski introduces the dynamic Chigorin Defence against the Queen's Gambit. ChessBase Magazine 233 rounds off the selection with up-to-date opening ideas, annotated games by top players and a wide range of training material. The products combine practical recommendations for tournament play with suggestions for independent analysis. | All photos: ChessBase

rubriker.title: Emin Ohanyan and Jiang Haochen outperform rating favourites, top final standings at Atyrau Masters
rubriker._rss_content: Armenian GM Emin Ohanyan won the Atyrau Masters in Kazakhstan after finishing tied for first place with Chinese IM Jiang Haochen on 7/9. The 20-year-old Ohanyan, seeded 20th, claimed the title thanks to a superior tiebreak score, while 15-year-old Jiang, seeded 30th, secured three consecutive wins to catch the leader. Baadur Jobava took third place on 6½/9. | Photo: Kazakhstan Chess Federation

rubriker.title: Vahap Sanal and Team Türkiye triumph at NATO Chess Championship
rubriker._rss_content: Vahap Şanal won the 2026 NATO Chess Championship in Jūrmala with a perfect 7/7 score, while Türkiye took first place in the team competition. Slovenia's Laura Unuk finished second overall and was the event's top woman, with Germany's Robert Stein claiming bronze on tiebreaks. The championship brought together 148 military players from 18 NATO countries and also featured a blitz event won by Dutch IM Mark Timmermans. | Photo: Vladimir Lionter / @the_lionter

rubriker.title: FIDE President Timur Turlov meets Cyprus President Nikos Christodoulides in Nicosia
rubriker._rss_content: FIDE President Timur Turlov met Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides in Nicosia to discuss the country's growing chess infrastructure and future cooperation with FIDE. Cyprus has hosted several major international events in recent years while also expanding domestic tournaments, youth training and permanent facilities. The meeting highlighted the island's development as an emerging European chess centre and its potential as a model for combining elite events with long-term national growth. | Photo: FIDE

rubriker.title: US Championship: Round 9
rubriker._rss_content: Round 9 in Saint Louis left both sections with a clear leader and two rounds to play. In the open, Wesley So drew defending champion Fabiano Caruana in a sharp Italian and stays a full point ahead on 6.5/9, in a round with five draws and one decisive game. In the women's, rookie Rachael Li beat Nazi Paikidze after a late blunder to reach 7/9 and secure her first IM norm, while all six games were decisive.

rubriker.title: Cursos de Preparación de Profesores - octubre a diciembre de 2026
rubriker._rss_content: La Comisión de Ajedrez en la Educación de la FIDE mantiene activa su oferta de formación para docentes con una nueva serie de cursos programados entre octubre y diciembre de 2026. Coordinados por Alla Khachatryan, estos programas buscan ampliar la comunidad internacional de instructores certificados mediante formación pedagógica, herramientas digitales y recursos educativos destinados a integrar el ajedrez de manera estructurada en distintos contextos de enseñanza. | Foto: Cortesía de Alla Khachatryan

rubriker.title: Total Chess pone sobre la mesa un sistema unificado de ratings Elo
rubriker._rss_content: Total Chess ha propuesto un nuevo sistema de puntuación que combina los ratings de los jugadores en ajedrez clásico, rápido y blitz en una sola cifra. Desarrollada por el investigador Mehmet Mars Seven en colaboración con Norway Chess, la fórmula utiliza las puntuaciones Elo existentes de la FIDE para evaluar la fuerza de juego global de los ajedrecistas en las tres modalidades. Magnus Carlsen (en la imagen) encabeza la clasificación inaugural, seguido de Hikaru Nakamura y Nodirbek Abdusattorov. El sistema será sometido a una consulta pública antes de introducir posibles modificaciones. | Foto: Nils Rohde / ChessBase
